title: Tino Livramento likely out for rest of Newcastle season, in line to be fit for World Cup – Eddie Howe
content:
Tino Livramento is unlikely to feature again for Newcastle United this season, but is in line to be fit for the World Cup if selected in the England squad.

The 23-year-old, who has had an injury-disrupted season, has missed Newcastle’s last two games with a thigh problem.

While the issue is not serious and the right-back could return for Newcastle’s final match of the campaign at Fulham, Eddie Howe, the head coach, is keen not to rush Livramento back and so it seems likely he will sit out the final three fixtures.

Theoretically, therefore, Livramento could go to the tournament held in the United States, Canada and Mexico with England, if Thomas Tuchel selects him.

“Tino’s doing well, he’s back running on the grass,” Howe said ahead of Newcastle’s trip to Nottingham Forest on Sunday. “I don’t think he’ll be back this season. We could possibly push him for the Fulham game, but I think that’d be silly on his behalf, so let’s let him recover and have a good summer.”

Lewis Miley, meanwhile, has undergone successful surgery on a broken leg, having slipped in training on Tuesday.

Howe is hopeful that, despite the fractured fibula, Miley will be fit enough to be involved in at least some of Newcastle’s pre-season ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

“It was a really innocuous moment training on Tuesday,” Howe said on Friday. “There was no-one around him, no other play involved and he slipped. At that moment we thought maybe a twist, but he was unable to continue and we realised it was more serious than we thought.

“He faces a few months out, we hope he’ll be back in and around pre-season. It’s a real shame because he was playing really well, a real blow for us but also for Lewis. But knowing his strength of character, he’ll be back better than ever.

“It’s been a huge frustration for him. He’s had some really unfortunate moments. This was a slip, there was nothing he could have done about it. We’ve tried to manage his workload, we’re aware of his age and we’ve tried not to overload him too much. Athletically he is outstanding and his body is strong, but he’s still growing to a degree.”

It is uncertain whether Fabian Schar, the centre-back, who has not featured since the 4-3 victory over Leeds United on January 7, will play again this season.

The 34-year-old, who is out of contract in June, suffered ankle-ligament damage and then contracted an infection in his foot, but is back training.

“It’s not 100 per cent sure,” Howe said, when asked if Schar would feature again this season. “His situation was unique because he was close to returning to full fitness and then got this infection. He is looking stronger in his body, but if he is going to be able to return before the end of the season is unsure.”
